guidance:
# Cell-Tracking Guidance for ELEPHANT Agent

**Dataset context:** This is a sparse (25–35 cells/frame), 2D monolayer culture imaged over 92 timepoints with progressive crowding (t=0–39 sparse; t=52–91 confluent). A field-of-view shift occurs around t=39, and uneven illumination affects edge cells in early frames.

**Patch-boundary artifact risk:** YES — current 384×384 patches tile a 1100×700 image with non-integer division (1100/384 ≈ 2.86, 700/384 ≈ 1.82), creating irregular boundary zones. Expect spurious spot clusters aligned with patch edges in sparse background regions, especially in the right and bottom margins. **Reduce patch size to 320×320×1** (aligned to 16-voxel multiples, fits GPU memory for 2D+time, minimizes tiling artifacts, and stays well within image bounds).

**Self-training loop caution:** Cells are sparse and increasingly overlapped by t=52+; true achievable completeness is likely **0.70–0.75** (crowded regions will have genuine missed or merged detections). Chasing the generic 0.8 target will waste 2–3 refinement rounds on diminishing returns and risk detector instability (false positive inflation). **Lower max iterations to 2 and set completeness target to 0.72** to avoid burnout.

**Avoid merging nearby cells as single spots in crowded frames (t>50);** enforce strict intensity-valley separation to preserve individual tracks through confluent patches. Watch for the FOV discontinuity around image set boundary; if stage drift caused a true jump, pre-link candidates across that boundary only if motion model explicitly allows large displacements.
